comment:
Fix round on the composed render (the hero shot looks down Pike Street at the sign, sunset behind it). Keep the footprint, plot, site orientation and everything that works (the arcade stalls, the white market building, the lanterns). Fix:
1. The sign is a huge square stone billboard. The real PUBLIC MARKET CENTER sign is WIDE AND SHALLOW, about twice as wide as tall, standing on a light steel frame (iron bars / light grey walls) on the roof at the south corner: the words in big red neon letters (red stained glass panes or red concrete letters with glowstone/shroomlight right behind them so they glow), PUBLIC MARKET on the top line and CENTER on a lower, shorter line, the letters on a cream/white open frame rimmed with bulbs (end rods or lanterns). No solid stone panel behind it: you see sky between the letters and through the frame. Keep its top no higher than about 18 blocks above the roof, and face it up Pike Street (toward +x/+z) as now.
2. The clock is separate, below the sign at the corner: a round white clock face (white concrete, a black hand of iron bars/blackstone) about 5 blocks across with a red neon ring (red stained glass with light behind) and PUBLIC MARKET on it, hung from the building corner above the entrance; under it the MEET THE PRODUCER sign band.
3. The downhill west face and the long North Arcade sit on blank grey stone walls many blocks tall. Where a face is above the ground, it must be building, not retaining wall: on the west (low x) side give the Down Under levels tiers of windows (glass panes in white frames, some lit) on white-painted brick, storey lines every 4-5 blocks; only the part actually below the neighbouring ground may be plain foundation.
4. The North Arcade roof is a very dark heavy strip. Make it read as a light covered market: a light corrugated roof (light grey/white concrete slabs or smooth stone slabs with a lighter ridge), green-painted posts (green concrete / oak fences stained green), open sides showing the craft tables and string lights (lanterns) under it.
summary: I rebuilt the PUBLIC MARKET CENTER sign as a wide, open neon frame and replaced the corner clock with one 5-wide neon clock, with a MEET THE PRODUCER band under it. The Down Under and North Arcade west faces are now white brick with tiers of glazed windows, and the North Arcade has a light slab roof on green posts, open on both sides. I changed the generator parts and re-ran it into build.nbt; v1.nbt is untouched. Renders confirm the sign reads, open to the sky; the window glow can't be seen because the renderer has no lighting.
applied: 1 Sign (parts/landmarks.mjs): the solid billboard is replaced by an open frame of white_concrete rails and stiles, with end_rod bulbs every other cell. PUBLIC MARKET runs across the top box (z 256..310) and CENTER sits in a shorter lower box centred under it. The letters are red_stained_glass with glowstone directly behind, held on a thin iron_bars lattice, so you see sky between them. It stands on iron_bars legs: on the roof deck, and north of the corner block down onto the arcade shed roof, because 13 letters need 55 blocks of width. It is 55 wide by 17 tall (about 3:1, a little wider than the 2:1 you asked for), its top is at y 60 (18 above the roof), and it still faces east up Pike Street.

2 Clock: one round clock about 5 across hangs proud of the set-back wall on the corner pier (x 41, y 35..39, z 305..309), above the corner entrance. It has a white face, black hands and a red stained-glass neon ring with glowstone set into the wall behind it. Under it, a dark oak MEET THE PRODUCER band runs along the corner fascia at y 30, with three glowing hanging signs below it. The board that used to sit on the parapet has been moved there, because it was hiding CENTER; the parapet is now continuous.

3 West faces: the Down Under windows had been walled over (the shell was solid, so the facade glazing was refused). Now the shell opens 3x3 windows in every 6-bay at each level that clears the ground, on the west faces, the north-facing step faces and the south face. It glazes them and puts ochre_froglight behind about 4 in 5. The wall is quartz_bricks above a cobbled_deepslate plinth that stops at ground+1, with grey storey lines at y 7, 12 and 17. The North Arcade's west face (x 28) now goes down to the lower neighbouring ground (the 7x7 column west of it) as white brick with storey lines at y 8 and 13 and 2x3 lit windows; only the part below that ground is plain foundation.

4 North Arcade roof (parts/roofs.mjs): the dark deepslate gable is replaced by a hand-laid low gable of smooth_stone slabs in half steps, with a white smooth_quartz slab ridge and hanging lanterns on chains under the ridge every 4 blocks. The west wall x 29 is now open green_concrete posts with a head beam and a dark oak fence rail, so both sides show the craft tables.
skipped: The words PUBLIC MARKET on the clock face: 13 letters can't fit on a 5-wide dial, and banner or sign letters would have to hang at x 42, which is off the plot. The words are on the sign above it instead.
The south clock face was removed rather than restyled. You described one clock, and two clocks side by side on the corner read as a pair of eyes in the render.

Things I noticed but left alone because you didn't mention them: roof.json was never written, so the Main Arcade (R-C) has no pitched roof and its two chimney stacks float (check reports them). The corner arcade storey has no posts at x 41. The North Arcade hall roof (z 133..160) and the street shed roof are still dark slate. The end_rod bulbs on the white frame get a light-on-light warning from the palette check (they are meant to glow at dusk).
